theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.GaussianForms.integral_pow_four_stdNormal / integral_cube_stdNormal / integral_sq_stdNormal / variance_linear_add_sq_stdNormal / stdNormalPi_map_orthonormalBasis / form_stdNormalPi / form_gaussianImage

theorems.informal: E x^2 = 1, E x^3 = 0, E x^4 = 3 for N(0,1); Var(a x + b x^2) = a^2 + 2 b^2; rotation invariance of the standard normal vector; mean/variance of c0 + a^T x + x^T Q x for standard normal x (Q symmetric) and for z = M x.

paperIssues: The lemma 'Variance of Gaussian Forms' itself is correct as stated; the paper gives no proof ('standard results'), a complete proof is formalised. The hypothesis ||C||_2 < infinity is vacuous for a finite matrix; positivity of C is not needed for either inequality.

Diagonal D is more restrictive than necessary (symmetric suffices), but symmetry cannot be dropped: for non-symmetric D the correct formula is Var(z^T D z) = 2 tr((C (D+D^T)/2)^2), not 2 tr((CD)^2) (numerically 107.7 vs 54.1 on a random instance), and the inequality tr((CD)^2) <= ||C||_2^2 tr(D^2) is false (C = diag(1,0), D = [[0,1],[-1,0]] gives 0 <= -2); formal counterexample GaussianForms.not_trace_mul_sq_le_of_not_isSymm.

Gap at tex l.1022: the proof says the variance of s^S_{t+1} 'is the variance of the sum of the linear and quadratic forms' and cites the lemma, but the lemma only gives the two variances separately; the cross term 2 Cov(g^T z, z^T D z) is not addressed. It is in fact 0 (proved: IsCenteredGaussian.covariance_linear_quadratic), so Var(s^S_{t+1}) = g^T C g + 2 tr((CD)^2) exactly.

The claim 'By Lemma gauss-var and Assumption 1, Var(s^S_{t+1}) = O(|S|)' does not follow from Assumption 1 as stated. The quadratic part 2||C||^2 tr(D_S^2) = 2 eta^4 ||C||^2 sum_S lam_i^4 is O(|S|) (block moment p=4, given ||C||_2 and eta bounded). The linear part ||C|| ||g_S||^2 = 4 eta^2 ||C|| sum_S lam_i^4 (1-eta lam_i)^2 c_i^2 is a weighted energy that Assumption 1 does not control, because sup_i lam_i is not assumed bounded. Counterexample satisfying all four items of Assumption 1: d = 2k, lam_1 = k^(1/8), other dominant lam_i = 1, bulk lam_i = 1/2, c_1^2 = d, other c_i = 0, C = diag(1/2,0,...,0): Var(s^D_{t+1}) ~ 2 eta^2 k^(1/2) (1 - eta k^(1/8))^2 d, of order d^(7/4), and E[s^D_{t+1}]/k diverges, so l'_D is not finite either. With an additional uniform bound on lam_1 the O(|S|) bound holds (Spec.variance_sNext_le_lam1_of_isCenteredGaussian). Under Assumption 1 alone one still gets Var = O(d^(7/4)) = o(|S|^2), which suffices for the Chebyshev step but not for Lemma wlln-blocks as stated (this last asymptotic statement is argued in the fidelity note, not formalised).

The trace assumption 'Tr(Sigma) in (0, infinity)' is ambiguous. What the variance bound needs is ||C||_2 = s_max bounded uniformly in d. If the trace is only finite for each d (e.g. Sigma = d I) no O(|S|) bound holds. If it is bounded uniformly in d, then ||C||_2 <= tr C (proved) but the noise becomes asymptotically invisible: e_S <= max_S lam_i^2 * Tr Sigma = o(|S|), so the limits l'_S = lim E[s^S_{t+1}]/|S| do not depend on the noise; isotropic noise Sigma = sigma^2 I is excluded by a uniform trace bound although it has bounded s_max.

Relative to (E s_{t+1})^2: the transfer E[theta_{t+1}] - thetaBarNext -> 0 needs Var(s^S_{t+1})/(E s_{t+1})^2 -> 0. This holds (rate 1/d with bounded lam_1, d^(-1/4) under Assumption 1 alone) only if E[s_{t+1}]/d has a positive limit; positivity of the limits (the paper's y_0 in (0, infinity)) is asserted without proof, and Assumption 1 even allows lam_{B,p} = 0.
eta_t = O(1) is used implicitly in the O(|S|) claim but is not part of Assumption 1.

Mean, variance and Cov = 0 all come out of one master statement (IsCenteredGaussian.affine_quadratic_form). Numerical checks with numpy were run before formalising.

Definitions introduced in this file (not in Defs.lean): SuspiciousAlignment.IsCenteredGaussian; GaussianForms.stdNormalPi, gaussianImage, mgfDeriv; GaussianForms.chi, gVec, dVec (the paper's chi_{S,t}, g_{S,t}, D_{S,t}). An anonymous instance IsProbabilityMeasure (gaussianImage M) is declared.
